name: Jahresring
prior: Strike position on a modal bar is standard physical modelling: Csound 'marimba' opcode has ipos = strike position 0..1 (Perry Cook STK ModalBar; VS: csound.com/manual/opcodes/marimba), Mutable Instruments Rings 'Position' = where the structure is excited (VS: perfectcircuit.com/mutable-instruments-rings.html, schneidersladen.de, modulargrid.net), AAS Chromaphone lists 'hit position' among its resonator controls (VS: fullcompass.com/prod/227757, applied-acoustics.com/chromaphone-3/manual listing; manual itself unreachable here). Clock-driven change: Brian Eno / Peter Chilvers 'Reflection' app (2017) changes its rules with the time of day (brighter harmony in the morning, thinning and slowing in the early hours) and 'subtly with the seasons' (VS: generativemusic.com/reflection.html, avclub.com 1798256494, factmag.com 2016/12/15) - composition rules, not an instrument's timbre, and wall clock, not played time. Aging: Pianoteq 'Condition' slider since 4.5 'ages a piano on the fly', mint..worn (VS: forum.modartt.com id=5231, zynthian.org engine-pianoteq) and Eventide Instant Phaser Mk II 'Age' knob (component drift; VS: long-mcquade.com 348711) are manual sliders; an LV2 piano 'Lost Isle' (2016 linux-audio-user post) is described as sounding used/out of tune by play - a mailing-list anecdote (VS: lists.linuxaudio.org 2016-June/105360). Tree rings: Bartholomaeus Traubeck 'Years' (2011/12) reads a trunk slice's rings with a camera on a turntable and maps thickness/texture/colour to piano notes in Ableton (VS: core77.com/posts/21601, newatlas.com 21198, laughingsquid.com) - sonification, not an aging instrument. Games change music by hour/season (Animal Crossing, Proteus; A). In Myzel no struck engine uses y as a position: glo/mem/klb/gng scale decay, index, brightness, chirp with y (APP 3612-4580). Not found: a struck instrument whose timbre runs on a year clock of played time and ages irreversibly by hit count.
costNotes: Native: noise burst (BufferSource 0.03) + 4 bandpass biquads with mode gains (the measured 16-biquad bank is 1.64 units, i.e. about 0.1 per biquad+gain; R: webaudio.md section 4) = 0.4 + box lowpass + tube bandpass 0.15 + mixes 0.06 + autumn leaf noise/bandpass 0.1 when active = 0.65-0.75; the idea's 0.55 assumes 0.06 per biquad. Cheaper variant: sine oscillators per mode with setTargetAtTime decays as Membran does (mem = 0.4 units, APP 3649) and a 2-6 ms noise click - the beam-mode weights apply identically, only mallet-hardness colouring is lost, about 0.5. L3 (6 modes, 2 bars +-3 ct, tube per side): 1.2-1.4. Season/age state is a few floats on A.season in the main thread, free; ramps for the Saft glide and the Winter mode shift are setValueAtTime/setTargetAtTime per hit. Beam modes checked (sim/bio2_sim.py): free-free Euler-Bernoulli weights at x = 0.776 are 0 / 0.50 / 0.66 / 0.47 (fundamental gone, nodal line audible), at the centre 0.61 / 0 / 0.71 / 0 (classic centre tone); nodes of modes 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4 lie at x = 0.644, 0.723, 0.776, 0.868, 0.906, 0.927, so the y sweep from centre to end passes six nodes - a continuous, audible timbral path. Winter +2 % on ratios = 34 cent, under the 35-cent cap only if the fundamental is excluded.
soundHeld: Jahresring is struck, so a held finger is a ringing bar: the mallet position is fixed at the hit and setY after it can only move the box/tube colour, setF glides the four mode frequencies (a ringing bar gliding is physically absurd but Membran does the same and it works). Timbre over minutes: spring (short, sappy +25 ct glide), summer (long), autumn (leaf noise, +-8 ct), winter (stiff modes +2 %, dull fundamental, ice-crack impulse) - audible as a slow colour change only if the player keeps hitting; a single held note shows one season. The wooden-bar family is new in Myzel (Kalimba = tines, Membran = drum, Glocke/Schale/Gong = metal, Saite = string), and Hoehe = mallet position is the first position control among the struck engines: the sweep through the nodal line is the strongest 10-second demonstration, far more than the seasons.
soundBurst: The native format: it is a mallet hit. Position, hardness (vel) and season give every Puls hit a slightly different bar, and autumn's leaf noise plus winter's ice crack make lanes rustle and crack. Caveat on rates: with A.season += 0.002 per hit a lane of 8ths at 120 bpm (960 hits in 4 min) runs the year about three times faster than the clock alone (80-second seasons), and the irreversible age alpha = 1 - e^(-n/600) saturates after about 10 minutes of lane play: then every Jahresring voice is permanently -12 ct, box x0.7, bark noise x2 for the session. The aging must be reversible (reset action, sleep resets) and the per-hit season step rate-limited (count hits per second, not per hit), and the -12 ct should be capped at -6 ct or kept off chords with other engines.
failureModes: Base sound = marimba/modal bar = ordinary; without the position sweep and visible season text a listener hears a dull Kalimba
Year of 4 min is too slow for a demo; the 'Jahreszeit fest' selector and a start mid-season are mandatory
Hit-driven season step: a dense Puls lane triples the year rate; irreversible age saturates in ~10 min of lane play and sours tuning (-12 ct) against other engines
Position at x=0.776 kills the fundamental: a melodic line played exactly on the nodal line loses pitch identity - fine as a colour, needs a floor of ~0.1 on mode 1 for melody
Four biquads per voice cost ~0.1 each measured, so the 0.55 estimate is low; L3 two bars + tubes approach 1.4
Year clock must freeze while audio sleeps or in background tabs; resume jumps would flip a season
Winter +2 % mode shift applied to the fundamental would detune the note by 34 ct; keep it on modes 2+ only
verdict: Rare: strike position on a modal bar is textbook physical modelling (Csound marimba ipos, Rings 'Position', Chromaphone 'hit position'), and clock-driven or aging instruments exist only as composition rules (Eno's Reflection) or manual sliders (Pianoteq Condition, Eventide Age), so the year-clock-plus-irreversible-aging struck bar is not found but each ingredient is. Native at about 0.65 units (L3 about 1.3) - four biquad modes cost more than the idea assumes; the Euler-Bernoulli weights check out (fundamental vanishes at x = 0.776, modes 2 and 4 at the centre), so Hoehe = mallet position gives a continuous, audible sweep that no Myzel struck engine has, and the wooden bar is a missing family. Musically it is a perfect Puls hit and a good held bar; the season/age layer is subtle and slow, and under a Puls lane the year runs 3x and the age saturates in ten minutes, so rate-limit the hit counter, make aging reversible, cap the detune and lean the identity on the position sweep rather than the calendar.
